method.renderer: Unreal Engine 5.8 offscreen Metal gameplay viewport
method.comparison_mask: baseline pixels above y=310 that were red-dominant dry canyon terrain

matched_frame_metrics.interpretation: The gameplay canyon is less chalky and orange, while greater bounded local contrast makes the surface breakup more legible without crushed black faces. These are descriptive image statistics, not a perceptual or photoreal acceptance threshold.

rejected_brackets: The first graph-default bracket reduced terrain mean luminance only to 0.6968 because the legacy steep-slope mask barely covered the rounded source walls.
The second bounded color-coverage bracket reached 0.6720 mean luminance but left the sun-facing wall too chalky.
Global exposure and lighting changes were not used because they would also alter water, raft, crew, and hazard readability.
visual_findings: An incommensurate 83 m secondary macro projection and two deterministic world-space fields reduce the single-square repeated response across the canyon.
The accepted surface shifts the former tan/orange wall toward a restrained blue-gray basalt response with bounded brown weathering.
The sun-facing left wall remains too smooth and bright because source geometry is still a rounded 30 m DEM approximation.
Vegetation remains sparse and repetitive, the water/shoreline composition remains provisional, and no named guide or art reviewer accepted this frame.
external_gates_remaining: rights-cleared higher-resolution terrain, lidar, stereo reconstruction, photogrammetry, or field-capture coverage for the playable reach
